question: What was the pedestrian path for devotees to wave in homage to Stupa called in Buddhist architecture?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Medhi.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asoka i**s responsible for building some of India's early** Buddhist structures (273-232 A.D).**
 
• **Stupas, Viharas, and Chaityas** are the** three principal architectural styles** connected to Buddhism in India.
 
• To** honor the stupa,** worshipers are to wave** medhis.**
 
• **Sopana** came up the** two staircases **toward Medhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Torana:**

 
 
• Similar to the gates of an** Aryan hamlet**, **toranas** were **ceremonial entrances** erected at key locations.
 
 
 
• **Anda:**
 
 
• The** hemispherical dome** is **Anda.**
 
 
 
• **Chattra:**
 
 
• The **chattra** is a** three-tiered stone or wooden umbrella **that is erected over a pedestal that once served as both the** village shrine and the vedic alter of sacrifice.**
 
 
 
• **Harmika: **
 
 
• **A square balcony **with a beautiful shape **enclosing a pedestal** is located on top of the dome.
 
 
 
• **Vedica:**
 
 
• The **wooden or stone railing **that surrounds the stupa is known as vedica.
